body: Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars owned Thursday night. In steady rain in Baltimore on Nov. 5, the Jaguars beat the Ravens 33-10, with Lawrence completing 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington.
Jacksonville is now 6-2 and leads the AFC South by three and a half games over Houston.
## Why fans are buying in

Lawrence came into the night leading the NFL in passer rating, according to CBS Sports, and he now has 18 touchdown passes against just four interceptions this season. That is the kind of efficient, mistake-free football the Jaguars have been waiting on since they drafted him first overall in 2021.

The team around him is winning too. Jacksonville forced three turnovers, has allowed 17 points in two games since its bye, and has won four of its last five. It was also the franchise's first Thursday night win in three seasons, played in front of a national audience.

This run builds on last season, when the Jaguars went 13-4 and won the AFC South. Lawrence threw for 4,007 yards and 29 touchdowns and added nine rushing scores in 2025. He is also signed long term after a five-year, $275 million extension in June 2024.

Lawrence is already a known name with fans. He ranked No. 43 on the NFLPA's year-end Top 50 player sales list for March 2024 through February 2025, which covers all licensed player merchandise. In our analysis, a quarterback leading a first-place team on prime time is exactly the setup that grows that pull. This is our view, not a sales figure.

subheadline: The 22-year-old scored three times in Montreal and became the fastest active NHL player to five career hat tricks.

body: Logan Cooley is scoring at a pace few young players ever reach. The Utah Mammoth center had three goals and an assist at the Bell Centre on Nov. 5, his second hat trick in four games.

It was the fifth hat trick of his career, and it came in his 228th NHL game. That makes him the fastest active player to five, two games quicker than Alex Ovechkin, according to Daily Faceoff. Montreal rallied to win 5-4 in overtime, but the night belonged to Cooley.
## Why fans are buying in

Two of his goals came on the power play, and all three came before the midpoint of the second period. He now has 11 goals this season, tied with Auston Matthews for fifth in the NHL, and 21 points in 17 games. Utah is 10-6-1.

Cooley has been a franchise building block from the start. He went third overall in the 2022 draft, made the NHL All-Rookie Team in 2024, and scored four goals in one game against Vegas last November, a first for the Mammoth. He also scored the team's first playoff goal last spring, and he helped the United States win gold at the 2025 World Championship.
The Mammoth have committed to him for the long run. His eight-year extension, worth $10 million a year, began this season.
In our analysis, a 22-year-old center putting up hat tricks for a young team in a new market is the profile of a jersey that keeps climbing. This is our view, not a sales figure.

title: Why Steven Stamkos's Predators Jersey Is One to Get Now
subheadline: His overtime power-play winner in Denver was the 247th of his career, tying Robitaille for fifth in NHL history.
description: Steven Stamkos scored an overtime power-play winner in Denver on Nov. 5, his 247th, tying Luc Robitaille for fifth all time. Why his No. 91 jersey is a buy.
searchIntent: Predators and hockey fans who saw Stamkos's milestone want to know where he ranks all time and which Stamkos jersey to get.
body: Steven Stamkos keeps climbing the record book. On Nov. 5 in Denver, he drew a penalty in overtime and then scored on the power play 2:18 into the extra period to give the Nashville Predators a 3-2 win over the Colorado Avalanche.
It was the 247th power-play goal of his career. That moved him past Phil Esposito and into a tie with Luc Robitaille for fifth in NHL history.
## Why fans are buying in
The win was Nashville's third straight, and it came on the team's fathers' trip, with players' dads in the building. The Predators have now beaten Colorado twice in less than two weeks.

Stamkos is still producing like a top scorer at 36. Last season he scored 42 goals in all 82 games, led the Predators, and ranked second in the league with 10 game-winning goals. He reached 600 career goals on Dec. 31, 2025.

His résumé is one of the best of his generation. Tampa Bay took him first overall in 2008, and he captained the Lightning to back-to-back Stanley Cups in 2020 and 2021. He signed with Nashville as a free agent in July 2024 on a four-year deal, and he has become a central figure in the team's push back up the standings.

In our analysis, a milestone night like this one reminds fans that they are watching an all-time great, and that kind of moment tends to bring out the jersey buyers. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look
Stamkos wears No. 91 in Nashville, the same number he made famous in Tampa. The banner above shows the Predators' bright gold home jersey, one of the boldest looks in hockey.

Every power-play goal from here moves him closer to the top four.
